generated_for: Grade A subset of the drug-discoverer roster

hubs.name: NobelPrize.org laureate pages
hubs.note: Four to five artifacts per laureate on a fixed URL pattern, confirmed across 1985/1988/1990/2018/2019/2023/2024. Full lecture PDFs also sit at nobelprize.org/uploads/<year>/<month>/<surname>-lecture.pdf. 12 Grade A people and ~12 more in the wider roster. The single cheapest bulk source in the project.

hubs.name: Eric Topol, Ground Truths (Substack)
hubs.note: Long-form interviews, transcribed, with a working scientist asking the questions. Already found for Kariko, Knudsen, Urnov, Liu and Drucker. Search the archive for the rest of the roster before doing anything else - it is one feed, many people.

hubs.name: NIH VideoCast
hubs.note: Downloadable lecture video with a stable archive: NIH Director's WALS lectures and NCI symposia. Found for Shokat, Rosenberg and Baker; Graham and Folkman are likely there too.

hubs.name: Lasker Foundation award essays
hubs.note: Each award carries a first-person essay, often published in Cell or JCI. Sofia's 'Enter Sofosbuvir' is the model: a full design narrative, free PDF. Found for Sofia, Druker, Negulescu, Brown/Goldstein, Knudsen.

hubs.name: JCI 'A conversation with ...' series
hubs.note: Long interview plus video, in a consistent house format. Found for Vagelos, Hobbs and Drucker; the series covers many more.

hubs.name: SfN History of Neuroscience in Autobiography
hubs.note: Full first-person career accounts as free PDFs. Snyder is in volume 6. Check the whole series for CNS people.

hubs.name: Science History Institute oral histories
hubs.note: Oral-history-grade long interviews with chemists. Confirmed for Langer. The obvious place to chase Elion, Djerassi, Lipinski and other historical med chemists.

offline_targets.what: Janssen Pharmaceutica archive, Beerse (Belgium): archives, a series of interviews, company publications, and 'Historical Record of Janssen Research Publications (1952-1990)'.
offline_targets.why: 850+ papers, 500+ presentations, 80+ medicines by one person. Not online; needs a direct request to the company archive.

offline_targets.what: Carl Djerassi papers (SC0348), Stanford Special Collections, 1952-2014.
offline_targets.why: Finding aid is online; the material is not.

offline_targets.what: Authored-works collection donated to the Johns Hopkins Historical Collection on his 2022 retirement.
offline_targets.why: Complements the SfN autobiography chapter, which is online.

offline_targets.what: Annual Nature Medicine essay series accompanying the Lasker Awards, ~2000-present, on creativity and taste in science.
offline_targets.why: Behind a publisher paywall and not indexed as a series. One of the best explicit statements of scientific judgement anywhere in this corpus - worth the effort to assemble in full.

Derek Lowe.notes: In the Pipeline blog, 2002-present, ~175 posts/yr. Also Chemistry World column at https://www.chemistryworld.com/derek-lowe/1294.bio and a digital feed at https://www.science.org/digital-feed/pipeline. Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Lowe_(chemist)
Derek Lowe.known_for: In the Pipeline, 2002-present: ~20 yrs of daily medicinal-chemistry judgement

Bruce Booth.notes: Blogging since 2011; paginated archive at lifescivc.com/page/N/. Article index: https://muckrack.com/bruce-booth/articles
Bruce Booth.known_for: LifeSciVC, 2011-present: company-building and portfolio reasoning made explicit

Pat Walters.notes: Blog moved from Blogger to GitHub Pages; Blogger remains as archive. Notebooks accompany posts. Chief Scientist at OpenADMET, adjunct UCSF, 2023 ACS Skolnik Award.
Pat Walters.known_for: Practical Cheminformatics: how to evaluate computational drug-discovery claims

Robert Plenge.notes: Categorised blog archive (drug discovery / human genetics / NRDD). Full-time BMS employee.
Robert Plenge.known_for: PlengeGen: human-genetics-first target selection, written up as a method

David Grainger.notes: DrugBaron blog moved to Forbes; 20+ Forbes articles. Original DrugBaron archive needs locating. Founded Funxional Therapeutics, Total Scientific, RxCelerate.
David Grainger.known_for: DrugBaron / Forbes: contrarian analysis of why developers make bad decisions

Dennis X. Hu.notes: Drug Hunter knowledge platform, 200+ R&D institutions. Ex-FLX Bio/RAPT and Genentech medicinal chemist. Stanford PhD.
Dennis X. Hu.known_for: Drug Hunter: structured case histories of approved and clinical molecules

Daniel Erlanson.notes: Practical Fragments, with Teddy Zartler. 15+ years of fragment-literature review.
Daniel Erlanson.known_for: Fragment-based lead discovery; 15+ yrs of critical fragment literature review

key_papers: Eroom's Law, Nat Rev Drug Discov 2012
Predictive validity in drug discovery: what it is, why it matters and how to improve it
When Quality Beats Quantity: Decision Theory, Drug Discovery, and the Reproducibility Crisis
Jack Scannell.notes: No personal blog. Reasoning lives in papers plus long interview transcripts. Etheros Pharma / Univ of Edinburgh.
Jack Scannell.known_for: Eroom's Law; the 'better-than-the-Beatles' and model-validity theories of R&D decline

Gertrude B. Elion.notes: Nobel lecture 'The purine path to chemotherapy' (8 Dec 1988), reprinted in Bioscience Reports 1989 and Angew Chem 1989. Oral history not yet located - check Science History Institute.
Gertrude B. Elion.known_for: Rational antimetabolite design: 6-MP, azathioprine, allopurinol, acyclovir

Sir James Black.notes: Nobel lecture title: 'Drugs from emasculated hormones: the principles of syntopic antagonism'. Lindau Mediatheque holds lecture recordings.
Sir James Black.known_for: Propranolol (beta-blockade) and cimetidine (H2) — receptor-led drug design, twice

Paul Janssen.notes: 850+ publications, 100+ patents, 500+ scientific presentations, 80+ medicines. Janssen Pharmaceutica Beerse holds an extensive archive plus a series of interviews and company publications; complete publication list in 'Historical Record of Janssen Research Publications (1952-1990)'. That archive is the prize and needs a direct approach - not online.
Paul Janssen.known_for: ~80 marketed drugs incl. haloperidol, fentanyl, risperidone, loperamide, ketoconazole

Carl Djerassi.autobiography: The Pill, Pygmy Chimps, and Degas' Horse (1992)
Carl Djerassi.notes: Carl Djerassi papers (SC0348), Stanford Special Collections, 1952-2014. Also wrote novels/plays. Science History Institute oral history not confirmed.
Carl Djerassi.known_for: Norethindrone — the first orally active progestin (the Pill)

Solomon Snyder.notes: SfN History of Neuroscience in Autobiography vol 6 chapter is a full first-person career account (PDF). 1000+ papers. Donated authored-works collection to JHU on 2022 retirement.
Solomon Snyder.known_for: Opiate receptor identification; receptor-binding as a screening paradigm

Christopher A. Lipinski.notes: Key primary artifact: the Adv Drug Deliv Rev Rule of Five paper and its 2001 reprint commentary. CDD webinar 'beyond the rule of 5' with Barry Bunin is a recorded discussion. No personal site.
Christopher A. Lipinski.known_for: Rule of Five — property-based reasoning about oral drugs

Akira Endo.notes: 'A historical perspective on the discovery of statins', Proc Jpn Acad Ser B 86:484-493 (2010) - open-access first-person account, the single best artifact. Died 2024.
Akira Endo.known_for: Compactin (ML-236B) — the first statin, from fungal screening

P. Roy Vagelos.book: Medicine, Science and Merck (Vagelos & Galambos, Cambridge UP, 2004)
P. Roy Vagelos.notes: JCI 'A conversation with P. Roy Vagelos' includes a video interview. Merck CEO 1985-1994.
P. Roy Vagelos.known_for: Ran the lab-to-market machine behind lovastatin; the Mectizan donation decision

Joshua Boger.book_subject: The Billion-Dollar Molecule (Barry Werth, 1994) and its sequel The Antidote
Joshua Boger.notes: CEO of Vertex 1989-2009. 'Founder Stories' YouTube video plus the 2023 STAT Q&A on Casgevy are the two best first-person artifacts.
Joshua Boger.known_for: Structure-based design as a company thesis; HIV and HCV protease inhibitors

Paul Negulescu.notes: 2025 Lasker-DeBakey, 2024 Breakthrough Prize, 2022 Shaw Prize, 2018 Warren Alpert - all with Van Goor and Hadida, and all carry acceptance remarks/lectures. Lasker page is the highest-value entry point.
Paul Negulescu.known_for: CFTR modulators (ivacaftor, tezacaftor, elexacaftor) via functional screening

Stephen W. Fesik.notes: 'Drugging Challenging Cancer Targets Using Fragment-Based Methods', Chem Rev 2025 - a full statement of method. Foundational: BCL-xL X-ray/NMR structure 1996 at Abbott. No lecture video located yet; check Vanderbilt and ACS channels.
Stephen W. Fesik.known_for: SAR by NMR; ABT-737 lineage leading to venetoclax; now MYC/RAS

Phil S. Baran.notes: Baran Lab site hosts group teaching materials/handouts. Co-founded Sirenas, Vividion, Elsie Biotechnologies, Elima. X handle not confirmed.
Phil S. Baran.known_for: Scalable synthesis and electrochemistry that changes what med chem can make

E. J. Corey.book: The Logic of Chemical Synthesis (Corey & Cheng, Wiley 1989)
E. J. Corey.notes: Nobel lecture title 'The Logic of Chemical Synthesis: Multistep Synthesis of Complex Carbogenic Molecules'. Book is on Internet Archive in full text - the single densest artifact of explicit synthesis reasoning available. Retrosynthesis introduced in Harvard Chem 115, from 1960.
E. J. Corey.known_for: Retrosynthetic analysis — the explicit logic of synthesis planning

Brian J. Druker.notes: 2009 Lasker-DeBakey Clinical award (with Lydon and Sawyers) - the Lasker page and JCI essay carry the reasoning. cptech page is a first-person account of his Gleevec R&D involvement. Book context: 'The Philadelphia Chromosome' (Jessica Wapner). No lecture video located.
Brian J. Druker.known_for: Imatinib — clinical champion of targeted kinase inhibition in CML

Charles L. Sawyers.notes: MSK Science Spotlight lecture (8 Apr 2020) is video. Four named enzalutamide-resistance mechanisms make his resistance-first reasoning unusually traceable. 2019 AACR Princess Takamatsu Memorial Lectureship.
Charles L. Sawyers.known_for: Imatinib resistance mechanisms; enzalutamide; resistance-first thinking

Kevan M. Shokat.notes: Unusually rich: video podcast, NIH Director's WALS lecture (Mar 2023), two long interviews. Best single reasoning artifact is the Cagan interview.
Kevan M. Shokat.known_for: Drugging KRAS G12C via the switch-II pocket; analog-sensitive kinase alleles

Craig M. Crews.notes: PROTAC origin: met Ray Deshaies 1998 at a Burroughs Wellcome retreat. Podcast tells the birth-and-evolution story directly.
Craig M. Crews.known_for: PROTACs — targeted protein degradation as a new modality

James E. Bradner.notes: TEDxBoston 2011 'Open-source cancer research' - the JQ1 open-sharing decision argued in his own words. Internet Archive copy is downloadable.
James E. Bradner.known_for: JQ1 / BET bromodomain inhibition; open sharing of probes; then ran NIBR

Stuart L. Schreiber.notes: Broad-MIT Seminars in Chemical Biology lecture 'Listening to Probes: Individuals and Populations'. Founding director of Harvard ICCB 1997.
Stuart L. Schreiber.known_for: Chemical biology as a discipline; FKBP/mTOR mechanism; many companies

William G. Kaelin Jr..notes: 'Publish houses of brick, not mansions of straw', Nature 545:387 (2017) - F1000Prime top recommended article for six months running. Nobel 2019 (with Ratcliffe, Semenza).
William G. Kaelin Jr..known_for: VHL-HIF oxygen sensing (belzutifan); also the field's sharpest writing on rigour

Judah Folkman.biography: Dr. Folkman's War: Angiogenesis and the Struggle to Defeat Cancer (Robert Cooke, 2001)
Judah Folkman.notes: Gave an NIH Director's Lecture 'New Directions in Angiogenesis Research'. Check NLM Profiles in Science for archived lecture video. Died 2008.
Judah Folkman.known_for: Angiogenesis as a therapeutic target — a hypothesis held against consensus

Sir Gregory Winter.notes: Nobel Chemistry 2018 (phage display of peptides and antibodies), shared with George Smith and Frances Arnold. Constructed from the confirmed URL pattern; validated separately. MRC LMB oral histories are a further target.
Sir Gregory Winter.known_for: Humanised antibodies and phage display — the route to adalimumab and beyond

James P. Allison.documentary: Jim Allison: Breakthrough (2019, dir. Bill Haney, narr. Woody Harrelson)
James P. Allison.notes: The core reasoning move: recognising CTLA-4 as a brake rather than a pedal. UC Berkeley CRL's 'Story of Yervoy' documents the path. Documentary premiered SXSW March 2019.
James P. Allison.known_for: CTLA-4 blockade — ipilimumab; the checkpoint concept

Carl H. June.a16z: BioEatsWorld podcast episode on the future of CAR-T
Carl H. June.notes: 2024 Breakthrough Prize. Documentary follows the Emily Whitehead case. Correction to roster: no memoir of his own located - the book-length account is the documentary plus third-party coverage.
Carl H. June.known_for: CD19 CAR-T cell therapy into the clinic

Steven A. Rosenberg.notes: NIH VideoCast holds a large archive incl. the symposium for his 50 years at NCI ('Past, Present, and Future of Cellular Immunotherapy'). Peter Attia episode #177 is a long-form interview. NIH VideoCast is downloadable and transcript-friendly.
Steven A. Rosenberg.known_for: Adoptive cell transfer, TIL therapy, IL-2 — decades of iterative clinical work

Katalin Kariko.memoir: Breaking Through: My Life in Science (2023)
Katalin Kariko.notes: NobelPrize.org carries lecture + interview + podcast per laureate - a constructible four-artifact set. Eric Topol's Ground Truths interview is long-form and transcribed.
Katalin Kariko.known_for: Nucleoside modification making mRNA therapeutically usable

Drew Weissman.notes: Nobel 2023 with Kariko. Constructed from the confirmed NobelPrize.org URL pattern; validated separately. Pair his account with Kariko's - the two tell the same decade from different sides.
Drew Weissman.known_for: Co-discovered modified-nucleoside mRNA; vaccine and therapeutic translation

Robert S. Langer.notes: Science History Institute Distillations interview is a proper oral-history-grade artifact. 40+ companies founded; the recurring question across interviews is how he picks problems.
Robert S. Langer.known_for: Controlled release and delivery; co-founder of Moderna and ~40 others

Pieter R. Cullis.notes: 'From lipids to lipid nanoparticles to mRNA vaccines' (Nat Rev Mater 2021) is a first-person narrative review and the best single artifact. 'The 60-year evolution of LNPs for nucleic acid delivery' (2024) is the long view. Book title not confirmed - remove the roster's book claim until verified.
Pieter R. Cullis.known_for: Lipid nanoparticles for nucleic-acid delivery (patisiran, mRNA vaccines)

Ugur Sahin.book: The Vaccine (Joe Miller with Sahin and Tureci, 2021)
Ugur Sahin.notes: 2022 Cesar Milstein Lecture (with Tureci) at MRC LMB. 'The Vaccine' was written with their cooperation plus 60+ interviews - effectively an authorised reconstruction of a year of decisions. BioNTech founded 2008 with Christoph Huber.
Ugur Sahin.known_for: mRNA cancer immunotherapy and the COVID-19 vaccine (with Ozlem Tureci)

Barney S. Graham.notes: The 2P proline-stabilisation story is the cleanest structure-based design reasoning in modern vaccinology. C&EN 'The tiny tweak behind COVID-19 vaccines' reconstructs the decision. Lecture 'Structure-based vaccines for respiratory viruses'. Video not yet located - check NIH VideoCast.
Barney S. Graham.known_for: Prefusion-stabilised antigen design (RSV F, spike-2P) — structure-based vaccinology

Stanley T. Crooke.notes: Hosts his own podcast (Patient Empowerment Program) - a continuous first-person feed. Founded Ionis 1989; previously Bristol Labs and head of R&D at SKB. n-Lorem treats n-of-1 patients.
Stanley T. Crooke.known_for: Antisense oligonucleotides as a durable drug platform

David R. Liu.notes: Six+ long podcast interviews plus recorded lectures. Founder of nine companies incl. Editas, Beam, Prime. His lectures narrate design reasoning step by step - the richest single target in the genetic-medicine group.
David R. Liu.known_for: Base editing and prime editing; Beam, Prime, Editas

Fyodor Urnov.notes: Coined 'genome editing' in 2005 at Sangamo. 100+ papers, 130+ patents. Also writes NYT op-eds. Known for extended automotive metaphors - his explanatory style is itself the artifact.
Fyodor Urnov.known_for: Genome editing as medicine; bespoke CRISPR therapies for n-of-1 patients

Michael J. Sofia.notes: 'Enter Sofosbuvir: The Path to Curing HCV' (Cell 2016, Lasker essay, free PDF) is a first-person design narrative - liver-targeted nucleotide prodrug logic laid out in full. Plus a book chapter 'The Discovery of Sofosbuvir'. Best-documented single molecule on the list.
Michael J. Sofia.known_for: Sofosbuvir — phosphoramidate prodrug design that cured HCV

Michael S. Brown.notes: Nobel 1985 with Goldstein. Their joint Nobel lecture and 50-year retrospective document a scientific partnership as a working method. A 2020 book covers their NIH start.
Michael S. Brown.known_for: LDL receptor pathway — the mechanistic basis for statins and PCSK9 drugs

Joseph L. Goldstein.essay_series: Annual Nature Medicine Lasker supplement essays, 2000/2001-present
Joseph L. Goldstein.notes: KEY: chairs the Lasker Awards jury since 1996 and has written an annual Nature Medicine essay series since ~2000 on creativity, elegance and taste in science - what makes an experiment 'elegant' or a body of work 'beautiful'. That series is one of the best explicit statements of scientific judgement in the corpus and needs collecting in full.
Joseph L. Goldstein.known_for: Co-discoverer of LDL-receptor regulation; sharp essayist on scientific taste

Helen H. Hobbs.notes: JCI 'A conversation with Helen Hobbs' includes video. Named lecture series: TNQ Distinguished Lectures 2019 (three cities), Harvard Bloch Lecture 2019, 107th Ricketts Lecture 2022. Dallas Heart Study outlier method is the reasoning to capture.
Helen H. Hobbs.known_for: PCSK9 and ANGPTL3 loss-of-function humans — genetics as target validation

Sekar Kathiresan.notes: Four+ long podcast interviews - unusually good for transcript mining. Targets from human genetics: NPC1L1, APOC3, ANGPTL3, PCSK9. Active on X.
Sekar Kathiresan.known_for: Human genetics to base-edited PCSK9/ANGPTL3 therapies

Daniel J. Drucker.notes: glucagon.com has served for years as the field's central repository - his own curated archive of foundational studies and integrative reviews. Highest-value self-maintained resource of anyone in the metabolic group.
Daniel J. Drucker.known_for: GLP-1 biology; the intellectual through-line to incretin drugs

Lotte Bjerre Knudsen.notes: 'Inventing Liraglutide' (ACS Pharmacol Transl Sci 2019) is a first-person invention account - C16 albumin-binding fatty acid side chain, then C18 diacid plus a DPP-4-resistant substitution for semaglutide. Acquired ACQ2 episode is a long-form design narrative. 2024 Lasker.
Lotte Bjerre Knudsen.known_for: Acylation design giving liraglutide and semaglutide their half-lives

Richard D. DiMarchi.notes: 20 years at Lilly Research Labs; discovered the active peptide of Humalog. The GLP-1/GIP single-molecule dual-agonist insight became tirzepatide. Shared the 2024 Bhaumik award with Knudsen. No dedicated lecture video located.
Richard D. DiMarchi.known_for: Insulin analogues (lispro); GIP/GLP-1 multi-agonist concept behind tirzepatide

Steven M. Paul.notes: The KarXT story is a clean case of reasoning about a shelved asset: xanomeline's M1/M4 agonism worked but peripheral cholinergic side effects killed it at Lilly; pairing with trospium (does not cross the BBB) rescued it 25 years later. Paul inherited the molecule at Lilly and later built the company around it. Ex-Lilly EVP science and technology / president of Lilly Research Labs; also co-founded Sage.
Steven M. Paul.known_for: Muscarinic agonism for psychosis (KarXT); candid on CNS attrition

John Hardy.notes: 1991 first APP mutation implicated in Alzheimer's, leading to the amyloid cascade hypothesis. ALZFORUM is the place his running commentary and revisions live - worth crawling as a venue, not just his page. Breakthrough Prize 2016, Brain Prize 2018, knighted 2022.
John Hardy.known_for: Amyloid cascade hypothesis from APP genetics; genetics-first neurodegeneration

David Baker.notes: NIH VideoCast 'The Coming of Age of De Novo Protein Design' (Dec 2022) is downloadable. The 'communal brain' framing of how his lab works recurs across interviews and is itself a reasoning artifact about running a research group.
David Baker.known_for: De novo protein design; designed binders and minibinder therapeutics

John M. Jumper.notes: Google DeepMind podcast episode (47 min, Hannah Fry) traces AlphaFold 1 to 3. Y Combinator episode covers the CASP14 turn. EBI talk covers the history of AlphaFold. Strong on what the model does NOT solve - useful negative reasoning.
John M. Jumper.known_for: AlphaFold2 — structure prediction at usable accuracy

Mohammed AlQuraishi.notes: Long-form essays: 'AlphaFold2 @ CASP14', 'The AlphaFold2 Method Paper: A Fount of Good Ideas', 'The Future of Protein Science will not be Supervised'. WordPress feed makes the whole archive machine-readable.
Mohammed AlQuraishi.known_for: Protein structure prediction; the field's most analytical essayist on ML in bio

Gregory Landrum.notes: Blog moved from Blogspot to GitHub Pages in Jan 2022; both halves needed for the full archive. Posts are Jupyter notebooks in the repo - reasoning as executable code, same as Pat Walters.
Gregory Landrum.known_for: RDKit — the open cheminformatics substrate of modern discovery

Roger M. Perlmutter.notes: The 'Approved' podcast traces Keytruda from origin to approval with interviews from the program leads; 'Leaders & Legends' covers rebuilding Merck's clinical development org across 140+ approvals. Both are decision-reasoning gold. Now CEO of Eikon.
Roger M. Perlmutter.known_for: Backed pembrolizumab when it was shelved; explicit about R&D portfolio reasoning

Mene Pangalos.notes: The 5R rubric (right target, tissue, safety, patient, commercial potential) plus a measured before/after: 4% of candidates completing Phase III in 2005-2010 vs 19% in 2012-2016. A rare case of a published decision framework with its own outcome audit. Two papers: NRD 2014 and NRD 2018.
Mene Pangalos.known_for: The '5R framework' — an explicit, published decision rubric for projects

Aled M. Edwards.notes: Founded SGC in 2004; with Richard Gold wrote the 2007 SGC Open Science Principles - the first biomedical research org to mandate sharing and eschew patenting, including on novel chemistry. The eLife open-notebook interview (with Rachel Harding and Matthieu Schapira) is the clearest statement of the position.
Aled M. Edwards.known_for: Open-science target discovery; argues publicly about incentives and duplication

Chas Bountra.notes: KEY: University of Oxford Podcasts hosts a dedicated speaker page - a whole archive of his recorded talks in one place. 80+ papers, 10 patents, 100+ invited lectures. Ran SGC-Oxford 2008-2020 pooling 9 pharma companies, 5 patient groups and academic labs, all data free. 19 years in industry before Oxford.
Chas Bountra.known_for: Open target validation and pre-competitive collaboration

Paul Workman.notes: CONFIRMED: he runs a blog, 'The Drug Discoverer', at the ICR. That plus the Chemical Probes Portal ('fitness factors for small molecule tools') makes him the closest thing to a Derek Lowe inside an academic drug discovery unit. Crawl the whole blog.
Paul Workman.known_for: HSP90 and other programs; prolific writer on how to run drug discovery well
